previous_audits.chain_closure_explanation: The channel expansion closes with the stated interval order, and an independent spectral-recurrence plus determinant/Hadamard-saturation argument proves the converse criterion. The runner's finite checks support, but are not used as, the universal proof.
previous_audits.claim_scope: For a supplied finite-dimensional unitary, complete rank-one frame, squared-modulus kernels, and selective read/reset schedule, the exact cadence-defect identity and the equivalence between all-positive-pair kernel closure and monomiality of the unitary were audited.
previous_audits.load_bearing_step: The load-bearing chain is Delta_mn = K_(m+n) - K_m K_n = D_B Ad_(U^m)(I-D_B)Ad_(U^n)D_B and, under all-time closure, recurrence forces |det K_1|=1 so Hadamard saturation makes K_1 a permutation.
previous_audits.notes_for_re_audit_if_any: A second auditor should recheck the simultaneous spectral-recurrence step and determinant saturation; no open repair target was identified.
previous_audits.verdict_rationale: The interval ordering is correct: with the n-step interval first and the m-step interval second, reset evolution is K_m K_n, and inserting I-D_B gives the stated interference channel exactly. Independently of the runner, spectral-torus recurrence gives U^(t_j) approaching the identity; closure then gives K_1^(t_j) approaching the identity, forcing |det K_1|=1, while Hadamard and nonnegative unit-sum columns force K_1 to be a permutation and U to be monomial. The supplied frame and reset semantics bound the physical interpretation but are explicitly inside the audited scope rather than hidden dependencies.
